sections.label: Saraj hostage negotiator career
sections.summary: Saraj, aged 72, spent his life keeping Singapore safe and was a chief hostage negotiator for Singapore Airlines hijacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Saraj, aged 72, spent his entire life keeping Singapore safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He was one of our chief hostage negotiators for both Singapore Airlines (SQ) highjacks.

sections.label: UOB analyst demographic time bomb
sections.summary: Last December, a UOB analyst declared Singapore's demographic time bomb will start ticking this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last December, a United Overseas Bank (UOB) analyst even declared that Singapore’s demographic time bomb will start ticking, right this year.

sections.label: Healthcare spending and senior schemes
sections.summary: Healthcare spending tripled in five years, and billions were set aside for the Pioneer Generation Package and Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, in five short years, we have tripled our healthcare spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, we have set aside many billions for our Pioneer Generation Package and are spending a lot more for our Silver Support Scheme.

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing funding
sections.summary: Three billion dollars was set aside for the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, calling for a kampung and city for all ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Six, we have set aside $3 billion for the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, a remarkable plan, which called for Singapore to be a kampung and city for all ages, with vast opportunities for our seniors.

sections.label: Regulations for seniors and caregivers
sections.summary: It lists changing regulations for affordable dignified living, regulations to help seniors monetise housing assets, and caregiver leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (a) Changing regulations to enable affordable, dignified living options for all seniors; (b) introducing regulations to help our seniors, especially our private estate residents, to monetise their housing assets; and (c) introducing caregiver leave.

sections.label: Costly homes for seniors
sections.summary: Homes with more autonomy, privacy and activities cost nearly $4,000 to $15,000 a month, unaffordable for most retirees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are homes where seniors have more autonomy, privacy and activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But they cost from nearly $4,000 to $15,000 a month, obviously not affordable for the vast majority of retirees, even those staying in private estates.

sections.label: Affordability and monetising seniors' assets
sections.summary: The passage states affordability matters as much as choices, and that regulations and laws must change to help seniors monetise assets to pay for options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Just as important as the choices is the affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must change regulations and laws to help our seniors monetise their assets to pay for them, and we must create these options now.

sections.label: Separate land use category
sections.summary: The passage states the Government can have a separate land use category for retirement or assisted living homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, the Government can have a separate land use category for retirement or assisted living homes.

sections.label: Lower land sale amounts
sections.summary: The passage states that with a separate land use category, land sales could fetch a lower amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With a separate land use category, land sales could fetch a lower amount.

sections.label: Retirement village legislation and GFA bonus
sections.summary: The passage states the Government can embrace legislation like the Australian Retirement Village Act and give a GFA bonus to selected older condominiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, the Government can embrace legislation similar to the Australian Retirement Village Act, which governs the relationship between retirement homes and the seniors staying in them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four, the Government can provide a gross floor area (GFA) bonus to selected older condominiums that want to be partially or fully transformed into a retirement village.

sections.label: Pearl Bank en bloc senior housing
sections.summary: The passage states many residents want to En bloc, and one option is adding 150 senior housing units above the car park while keeping the architecture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many residents want to En bloc, which requires land intensification, which will allow residents of Pearl Bank to top-up their lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And one exciting option is to intensify by building an additional 150 units of senior housing on top of their existing car park, and also building more facilities catered to seniors, while keeping the unique architectural makeup of the rest of the development.

sections.label: Banks and reverse mortgage loans
sections.summary: The passage states banks are not interested in secured loans in such quantum due to the razor-thin margin of reverse mortgages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But banks are not interested in lending them secured loans in such quantum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is because, given the razor-thin margin of reverse mortgages, the banks have limited interest in secured loans for less than $200,000-$300,000.

sections.label: Senior Care Leave proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes starting with four days of Senior Care Leave for a selected group of Singaporeans who are already caregivers for their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we depart quietly into the night, our loved ones' presence will comfort us through that inevitable journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I propose starting with four days of Senior Care Leave for a selected group of Singaporeans who are already caregivers for their parents.

sections.label: Hope Collective and Project Starfish
sections.summary: In the speaker's constituency, The Hope Collective and an elderly befriending programme called Project Starfish exist, and Hope Collective partnered Mummy Yummy to deliver vegetarian meals to the needy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, in my constituency, I have started something called The Hope Collective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, we have an elderly befriending programme called Project Starfish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Through Hope Collective, they have partnered another group called Mummy Yummy that delivers vegetarian meals to the needy.

sections.label: Lawyers advising seniors on LPAs
sections.summary: A pool of lawyers can educate and advise seniors on legal matters such as Limited Powers of Attorney, and there is a wish to move towards dementia readiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, we have a pool of lawyers who can educate and advise on legal matters for the seniors, such as Limited Powers of Attorney (LPAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We also want to move towards dementia readiness.

sections.label: Seniors working and labour supply
sections.summary: IPS 2014 results indicate many Singaporean seniors want to work after retirement, with 90% saying work brings financial independence, social connection and self-worth, while Oxford Economics reports shrinking labour supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The 2014 results from the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) indicate a large proportion of Singaporean seniors have expressed interest to continue working after the age of retirement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Ninety percent of the respondents have indicated that working is a good way to stay financially independent, connect with society and retain their sense of self-worth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The latest report by Oxford Economics said that Singapore's labour supply will shrink by 1.7% in the 10 years through 2026, and by 2.5% in the following decade after accounting for changes to the participation rate.

sections.label: Barriers to older worker employment
sections.summary: Barriers include employer stereo-mindset, skills mismatch, lack of job flexibility, technological barrier and lack of business incentives, and the speaker agrees with much of the 2016 MOH blueprint on employability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The barriers of entry would include stereo-mindset of employers, skills mismatch, lack of job flexibility, technological barrier and lack of incentives for businesses and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I agree with many parts of the 2016 blueprint report on Action Plan for Successful Ageing by the Ministry of Health (MOH), especially on employability with ageless workplaces and lifelong employability.

sections.label: Blueprint suggestions for older workers
sections.summary: Suggestions include redesigning jobs for flexibility, accessible training, a seniors-only job bank, reviewing the retirement age, career guidance, mindset change, job trials, recognising good employers and intergenerational harmony.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Suggestions from seniors and employers in this blueprint report include the following: redesign jobs to offer older workers greater flexibility, make training accessible and effective for older workers, set up a dedicated seniors-only national job bank to lifelong learning, review or extend the retirement age as some think it should be extended to 70 while some others feel it should be abolished entirely, provide good career guidance and transition programmes a few years ahead of the re-employment age, promote mindset change among employers on the value of older workers, allow older workers to try out jobs via internships or job trials, recognise employers who treat older workers well, and promote intergenerational workplace harmony.

sections.label: Volunteering in retirement planning
sections.summary: Volunteering should be part of Retirement Planning programmes, covering recreation, lifelong learning, HDB and condominium, and skills-based volunteering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (a) Retirement planning typically focuses on financial planning; modules on volunteering should be part of all Retirement Planning programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (b) Recreation can be made more meaningful with volunteering roles, such as being a swimming buddy with someone with a physical disability, being a singing coach in nursing homes, being a volunteer playing chess with youths in a drop-in centre and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (c) Lifelong learning volunteering is a way to transfer skills gained or to learn new skills, in this context, volunteering prepares one for a new career.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (d) HDB and private condominium volunteering is a great way to get more connected to the neighbours, especially in door-to-door canvassing, in collecting information about their environment or in patrolling their estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (e) Skills-based volunteering, where many adults who have indicated an interest in using their skills and experiences for volunteering is a good approach.

sections.label: Seniors living independently at home
sections.summary: Government policy prioritises supporting seniors to live independently in their homes and communities, requiring safe, accessible environments and seniors-friendly HDB flat design.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The priority of the Government's policy is to support seniors to live independently in their own homes and communities for as long as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Planning, designing and building local environments that are safe and accessible to seniors are, therefore, vital to supporting them to live in their own homes and local communities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Seniors-friendly adaptations in design inside HDB flats will enable many to continue living independently despite disability.

sections.label: Telecare, telehealth and transport for seniors
sections.summary: Telecare and telehealth help manage health conditions for independent living, and accessible, affordable, flexible transport is essential for mobility as people age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Telecare and telehealth services are also becoming increasingly recognised as effective ways to prevent or manage some health conditions that effectively facilitate independent living.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Researches have shown that roles that require physical activity engage the brain and provide social interaction that are especially good for individuals because multiple area stimulation appears to reduce the risk of dementia and promote brain health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, enabling people, as they age, "to get out and about" through the provision of accessible, affordable and flexible transport systems is essential for ease in mobility.

sections.label: Three complementary actions proposed
sections.summary: The speaker proposes three complementary actions: education, bolder use of the Maintenance of Parents Act, and supplementary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The hon Member Mr Henry Kwek proposed three policy changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose three complementary actions: education; bolder use of existing legislation, namely, the Maintenance of Parents Act (MPA); and supplementary legislation.

sections.label: Reverse mortgage and Will instruments
sections.summary: Seniors can reduce financial dependence on children and still leave legacies using two legal instruments: the reverse mortgage and the Will.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In principle, they can reduce their financial dependence on the children and still leave legacies to them using two legal instruments: the reverse mortgage and the Will.

sections.label: Changing a Will
sections.summary: A senior can change a Will at any time, so an unfilial child can be written out of it at any time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Will can be changed at any time by the senior.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means that an unfilial child can be written out of the Will at any time.

sections.label: Maintenance of Parents Act use
sections.summary: The speaker proposes bolder use of the Maintenance of Parents Act, which lets the Commissioner apply for and represent seniors or parents in proceedings or appeals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Secondly, I would like to propose a bolder use of the existing legislation, namely, the Maintenance of Parents Act (MPA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MPA empowers the Commissioner to make an application on behalf of seniors or parents and represent them in proceedings or appeal under the Act.

sections.label: MPA applications by Commissioner
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for Family and Social Development to confirm the number of MPA applications made by the Commissioner from 2010 to date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Family and Social Development confirm the number of such MPA applications by the Commissioner from 2010 to date?

sections.label: Section 6 MPA orders
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to share the number of orders made under section 6 of the MPA and urges provisions for salary attachment orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister for Family and Social Development also share the number of such orders that have been made out of section 6 of the MPA?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also urge the Government to make express provisions under the MPA to allow attachment orders to be made against the salaries of children, which leads me to my third point: supplementary legislation.

sections.label: Abolish presumption of advancement
sections.summary: The speaker proposes abolishing the presumption of advancement when an elderly parent transfers property to an adult son or daughter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, abolish the presumption of advancement in circumstances where an elderly parent transfers property to an adult son or daughter.

sections.label: Property transfers and penalties proposals
sections.summary: The speaker proposes voidable property transfers, evidentiary burden on recipients, immediate maintenance obligation, harsher penal sanctions and a compulsory savings scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we should provide for transfers of property to be voidable, at the option of the parent, in the event that the child fails to provide basic amenities or basic physical needs to the parent after the transfer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should legislate to place the evidentiary burden on the receiving party to show that he or she had not defrauded, coerced or exerted undue influence on his or her parent, that market consideration had been paid to the parent, and that such money had not been routed back to him or her.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should provide that the statutory obligation to maintain one’s parents arises immediately upon the transfer of the property from parent to child, by operation of law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sixthly, we can amend our penal laws to provide harsher sanctions against those who prey on the financially vulnerable, of which the seniors should, by default, form a category.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government could consider a compulsory savings scheme whereby a part of the CPF contribution is channeled into a new sub-account designated for the purchase of annuities for the maintenance of the member’s parents.

sections.label: Walter Woon 1994 Bill speech
sections.summary: Prof Walter Woon said in 1994 that the Maintenance of Parents Bill was not aimed at Singaporeans who support and love their parents without being told.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prof Walter Woon, from his speech during the Second Reading of the Maintenance of Parents Bill in 1994, said: “The Bill is not aimed at the majority of Singaporeans who know their duty, who know where morals point and who support and love their parents without having to be told.

sections.label: Seniors and inclusive society
sections.summary: The pledge embodies ideals, and seniors should be seen as contributors who help build a more inclusive society, not only as a disadvantaged group to care for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These ideals are embodied in our pledge which is why our pledge, that short collection of words, deeply resonates with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But when we speak of our seniors, it should not only be about taking care of the disadvantaged group, it should be about how we can also build a more inclusive society because that advances the cause of Singapore and all Singaporeans, because seniors can contribute and give back, not only consume and receive.

sections.label: Rising life expectancy and work
sections.summary: As life expectancy rises, people will need to work later in life, so choices should be created for how seniors want to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Inevitably, as life expectancy rise, people will need to work in some form till later in life to some extent, depending on productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Should we strive to create a rich tapestry of choices for our seniors to decide how they want to work, for how many hours in what ways?

sections.label: NGOs and seniors' tech literacy
sections.summary: NGOs could be engaged to raise seniors' technology literacy and mobile app usage, perhaps using a social impact bond to tie results to state spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, engaging on-government organisations (NGOs) to raise the technology literacy and usage of mobile apps by seniors, using perhaps a social impact bond to tie results to state spending to ensure maximum impact for our fiscal dollars.

sections.label: Unlocking seniors' workplace potential
sections.summary: To fully unlock the potential of seniors in the workplace, more must be done to create options for work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To fully unlock the potential of seniors in the workplace, we need to do more to create options for work.

sections.label: Discouraged workers and ageism
sections.summary: Almost 10,000 workers are classified as discouraged, having given up looking for a job, some due to sensed ageist discrimination in the labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, almost 10,000 workers are classified as "discouraged", meaning that they have given up looking for a job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some of them have given up due to what they sense is ageist discrimination in the labour market.

sections.label: Fighting ageism and health costs
sections.summary: More could be done to fight ageism, such as giving TAFEP more teeth and recognising employers with older workers, and to reduce disease burden through screenings and vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let us do more to fight this, perhaps by giving the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) more teeth and perhaps exploring how we can better recognise employers who walk-the-talk by having older workers make up a larger share of their workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is there more we can do upstream to ensure that the burden of disease, chronic conditions does not erode the quality of life of seniors and harm their potential contribution to the economy and drain state finances?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are pushing out subsided health screenings to all and this is a step in the right direction as is MOH's action plan for successful ageing and the various programmes associated with it, such as the Active Ageing Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is there more we could do, for example, to offer low-cost or free vaccines to citizens to reduce the risk of disease later in life, a move that would probably more than pay for itself, in terms of fiscal dollars and a subject which MPs have spoken about in the past?

sections.label: Health screening for seniors
sections.summary: MOH promoted and subsidised basic health screening since September 2017, making it free for Pioneer Generation and low cost for CHAS cardholders.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: A person's state of health is by far one of the strongest determinants in our ageing process.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I am heartened that MOH has widely promoted the need for basic health screening since September 2017 and heavily subsidised it.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While noting that cost and concern about the outcome of health screening are the main deterrents for many seniors, MOH has made the basic health screening free of charge for our Pioneer Generation, and at very low cost for Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) cardholders and other Singaporeans.

sections.label: MediSave limit for seniors
sections.summary: The proposal is to increase the MediSave usage limit on outpatient treatment for seniors aged 70 and above with chronic illnesses who met their Basic Healthcare Sum.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, to increase the MediSave usage limit on outpatient treatment for seniors aged 70 and above, those with chronic illnesses but have met their Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS).

sections.label: MediSave outpatient limit example
sections.summary: A senior with over $55,000 in MediSave can use only $400 for outpatient treatment, needing $800 out-of-pocket cash yearly for medication.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: With only $400 allowed to be used from his MediSave for outpatient treatment, he needs $800 out-of-pocket cash for his regular medication each year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But he still has over $55,000 in his MediSave account.

sections.label: Dementia among Singapore seniors
sections.summary: The 2015 WISE study showed that by 2030, one in 10 Singaporeans aged 60 and above may have dementia, an estimated 80,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: From the Well-being of the Singapore Elderly (WISE) study in 2015, it showed that by 2030, one in 10 Singaporeans aged 60 and above is likely to suffer from dementia.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: That is an estimated 80,000 seniors who may have dementia in their golden years.

sections.label: LPA awareness and fee waiver
sections.summary: Many seniors are unaware of LPA benefits, and OPG extended the LPA application fee waiver for two years till 31 August 2018 for LPA Form 1.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, many seniors are not aware of the benefits of an LPA and how to go about it.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I know that in order to encourage more Singaporeans to pre-plan to protect their interests, the Office of Public Guardian (OPG) has extended the LPA application fee waiver for two years till 31 August 2018, at least for those filing the LPA Form 1.

sections.label: Partnering senior day care centres
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider partnering senior day care centres within each neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As a start, I would ask the Ministry to consider partnering senior day care centres within each neighbourhood.

sections.label: 2-room flexi short lease flats
sections.summary: HDB could consider building 2-room flexi short lease flats within the same building as 3- or 4-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: HDB could consider if moving forward we can build the 2-room flexi short lease flats within the same building constituting 3- or 4-room flats.

sections.label: Motion on vibrant seniors
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Motion's emphasis on proactive action from prevention to social care for seniors' golden years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In order to have an "undefeated mind" and be physically healthy in our golden years requires proactive actions from early on.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I think this Motion is timely, from personal prevention to social activeness, senior-friendly townships to social care networks.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It is time we begin to work cohesively as a community towards achieving a country of vibrant seniors whom we treasure and, they, who can live their golden years in comfort.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I strongly support the emphasis for us to begin doing more as a nation towards this goal and, together, we will and can become sprightly seniors.

sections.label: Enhanced Screen for Life cost
sections.summary: The Enhanced Screen for Life programme costs $5 or less for eligible Singaporeans above 40.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Enhanced Screen for Life programme is $5 or less for eligible Singaporeans above 40.

sections.label: Dementia numbers and prevalence
sections.summary: People living with dementia here are expected to double by 2030, with about 10% prevalence among seniors aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The number of people living with dementia here is expected to double by 2030 and the prevalence of dementia is about 10% among seniors aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Elderly medical bills and subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to subsidise more mental illnesses, more CHAS benefits for lower-income groups, and supports ElderShield Review Committee recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Medical bills are one of the top concerns of the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge MOH to include a wider range of mental illnesses for subsidised treatment in our polyclinics and public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope the Government could consider more CHAS benefits for the lower-income groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the recommendations by the ElderShield Review Committee.

sections.label: Time banking for elderly volunteering
sections.summary: The speaker proposes time banking, where seniors' volunteering hours are deposited and exchanged for free or discounted PA courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To attract them beyond one-off projects and come out of their comfort zones on a sustainable basis requires greater logistical planning and financial support from the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to propose time banking to draw more elderly to our community volunteering programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, every hour of volunteering clocked by participating seniors can be deposited, accumulated and exchanged for free or discounted PA courses.

sections.label: MOE, PA, MOH senior support
sections.summary: MOE and PA can facilitate arrangements between schools and senior groups, and MOH is asked to consider implementing Community Network for Seniors in all constituencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) and PA can continue to assist by facilitating the arrangements between schools and senior groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that MOH will consider implementing Community Network for Seniors to all constituencies.

sections.label: Eldercare centres and leave
sections.summary: Eldercare centres could be augmented with short-term accommodation for seniors whose caregivers are temporarily unavailable, and the Government is urged to legislate eldercare and bereavement leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should also explore how services at our eldercare centres can be augmented to include short-term accommodation for seniors whose caregivers are temporarily unavailable due illness, work or travel overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I appeal again to the Government to legislate eldercare leave and bereavement leave.

sections.label: Barrier-free access in HDB flats
sections.summary: Barrier-free access has mostly been achieved in the heartlands, and the speaker wants the same in HDB flat designs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Barrier-free access has mostly been achieved in our heartlands and I really would like to see the same in the designs of our HDB flats.

sections.label: Drama Box end-of-life care work
sections.summary: The speaker declares that his theatre company Drama Box and he have been actively working on end-of-life care, presenting creative projects reaching the elderly and other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, thank you for allowing me to speak on this Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, while some of my colleagues are putting on the earpiece for translation, I will make a declaration that my theatre company Drama Box and myself have been actively working on this issue of end-of-life care, presenting quite a lot of creative projects that reach out to the elderly and other sectors of the society.

sections.label: Man's retirement and dementia
sections.summary: A man who was not highly educated and had few hobbies retired over 10 years ago and began experiencing dementia five years after retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He was not highly educated, neither did he have any hobbies in particular, except for playing a game of mahjong or enjoying some drinks with his friends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He retired more than 10 years ago and, five years after his retirement, he started experiencing the onset of dementia.

sections.label: Rising public healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: Public healthcare expenditure more than doubled in five to six years to $10 billion in FY2016, and will have to increase further as the population ages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Public healthcare expenditure more than doubled over the past five to six years, reaching $10 billion in financial year (FY) 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our society believes in each generation financing its own needs, not wanting to burden our children’s generation and the next.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: However, as our population continues to age, healthcare expenditure will still have to increase to fund enhanced or new elderly programmes for the larger base.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Also, infrastructural investments, retrofitting and hardware maintenance will still be needed to create an elderly-friendly environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Given our expectations on social spending, it is imperative that we maximise the impact of every dollar spent.

sections.label: R&D funding for digital eldercare
sections.summary: Speaker asks for an update on fund utilisation for R&D and startups in digital eldercare solutions, noting MOH's elderly-focused innovation funding scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It would be most ideal if Singapore can leverage our own existing competencies in research and development (R&D) to develop solutions for ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I understand that MOH had introduced a funding scheme to encourage elderly-focused innovations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask for an update on the utilisation of funds to support R&D efforts and startups looking into digital eldercare solutions.

sections.label: Community Networks for Seniors pilot
sections.summary: Speaker notes the Community Networks for Seniors pilot has helped provide comprehensive services and hopes it can be rolled out nationally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: At present, I am aware that the Government has piloted the Community Networks for Seniors and it has been very helpful in providing a suite of comprehensive services for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope this scheme can be rolled out nationally so that all seniors can benefit from it.

sections.label: National coordinating body for volunteers
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether a national coordinating body could consolidate community needs and resources and coordinate volunteer roles and manpower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could there be a national coordinating body for volunteers in Singapore that consolidates and monitors the list of needs in the communities and resources that are already available, identify the roles and corresponding manpower needed, coordinate and help everyone clearly see how they can fit in to help?

sections.label: Optimising work for senior workers
sections.summary: Speaker suggests government test optimising work environments, job roles and benefits for senior workers, expand recruitment, and introduce decentralised elderly health programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government can take the lead in testing how the work environment, workflows, job role designs and even compensation and benefits, such as health benefits, can be optimised for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Can we expand it to recruit more and cover more functions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Third, introduce health programmes tailored to meet the needs of the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Decentralise the implementation of these programmes, cascade them down to the precinct or even to the individual HDB blocks.

sections.label: Supporting successful ageing
sections.summary: Speaker says seniors' wisdom and legacy are a gift and support must be strengthened for successful ageing, then shares in Mandarin his father's dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Their wisdom, resilience and this legacy that they have built for Singapore are a gift to us and our young.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We must, therefore, strengthen our support to enable successful ageing and create an environment where our seniors can continue to thrive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   My father retired more than 10 years ago and, five years after his retirement, he started experiencing the onset of dementia.

sections.label: Chinese words describing decline
sections.summary: Speaker lists Chinese terms such as shuai ruo, shuai tui and shuai bing that describe weakness, decline, deterioration, withering and sickness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: For example, in Chinese, we say, "shuai ruo"(weak), "shuai tui" (to be in decline), "shuai yan" (to deteriorate in looks), "shuai ku" (to wither), "shuai hao" (to be waste away), "shuai jian" (to weaken), "shuai bing" (to become sickly).

sections.label: Elderly people's relationship groups
sections.summary: The speaker says he has met many old folks through his productions and categorises them into three groups based on their relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In recent years, I have met many old folks through my productions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: I categorise them into three groups: those who are very close to their friends and relatives; those who are on bad terms with their friends and relatives, and the third group, those who do not maintain relationships with anyone.

sections.label: Elderly care in Singapore and hometown
sections.summary: In Singapore families hire a domestic helper for elderly long-term care, while in her hometown a relative volunteers to care for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In Singapore, when an elderly family member falls ill and requires long-term care, the first thing that other family members would think of is to hire a domestic helper to help with caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In her hometown, there would always be a relative who will volunteer to take care of the elderly family member while the rest of the family will pay for the living expenses of this relative.

sections.label: Caregiver burden and government measures
sections.summary: The speaker describes caregiving as exhausting and thankless, notes his mother lost about 10 kilogrammes, and hopes the Government will consider two measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: She also did not want our father to become a burden to us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: However, despite getting help from a domestic worker to take care of my father, she still lost around 10 kilogrammes in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Caregiving is an exhausting and often a thankless job, but many people are unable to afford a maid and have to juggle between caregiving and work at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: They have to pay for transport and medical bills, they do not have enough rest as they have to look after the elderly for extended periods of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: This will not only affect the mental health of the caregiver but also those around him or her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: I listened to the suggestions by many of my Parliamentary colleagues and I agree with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider two measures to help reduce caregivers’ burden.

sections.label: Three areas concerning elderly residents
sections.summary: The speaker says he will touch on three areas raised by elderly residents: financial sustenance, mental wellness and community support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to touch on three areas which have been raised as concerns by some of my elderly residents and my observations of the efforts in place to help the elderly: one, financial sustenance; two, mental wellness; and three, community support.

sections.label: Reviewing Lease Buyback Scheme
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Lease Buyback Scheme could be expanded to bigger flats such as 5-room and executive flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One area that could be reviewed is the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could there be further expansion of this scheme by extending it to bigger flats, such as 5-room and executive flats?

sections.label: Reviewing CHAS for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker says CHAS should be reviewed to help improve the financial circumstances of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Another scheme which should be reviewed to help improve the financial circumstances of seniors would be CHAS.

sections.label: CHAS cards for seniors
sections.summary: A request is made to raise the CHAS income ceiling or increase subsidies so more elderly residents qualify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The CHAS cards are precious and meaningful for the seniors and the scheme goes a long way in helping them with their expenses, especially for those who have to seek regular medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, request that some adjustments be made, for example, to raise the income ceiling so that more elderly residents would qualify for CHAS or to increase the subsidies available within the scheme.

sections.label: Commissioner cases settled by conciliation
sections.summary: Over 80% of cases referred to the Office of the Commissioner from 2014 to 2016 are settled through conciliation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over 80% of the cases that are referred to the Office of the Commissioner from 2014 to 2016 are settled through conciliation.

sections.label: Community Network for Seniors extension
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to extending the Community Network for Seniors for systematic collaboration between Government agencies and community stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Various agencies should also join in this effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, look forward to the extension of the Community Network for Seniors which aims to enable a more systematic collaboration between Government agencies and community-based stakeholders.

sections.label: Belanja-A-Meal scheme at coffee shop
sections.summary: The Belanja-A-Meal scheme, a coffee shop and Residents' Committee collaboration, is extended to all needy residents in the zone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Recently, we also introduced the "Belanja-A-Meal" scheme at one of the coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This scheme, which is a collaboration between the coffee shop and the Residents’ Committee (RC), is extended to all needy residents within the zone.

sections.label: Lease Buyback and CHAS enhancement
sections.summary: The Lease Buyback Scheme and CHAS must be continuously enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Lease Buyback Scheme and CHAS, for instance, must be continuously enhanced.

sections.label: Ageing well and dignity ecosystem
sections.summary: The speaker says it is in our interests to invest in an ecosystem for seniors to age well, noting those above 65 will equal those under 15.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We will all be that statistic, that group that would tap on Government funds, that would add to healthcare costs, that would need to be cared for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, in our interests to invest and build an ecosystem that would allow for seniors to age well and with dignity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the first time in our history, the number of people aged above 65 will equal those aged under 15.

sections.label: Social safety net for seniors
sections.summary: The Government has strengthened the social safety net for seniors, including the Silver Support Scheme, and MediShield Life addresses most general healthcare concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the past few years, the Government has strengthened the social safety net for our senior citizens, such as the Silver Support Scheme, among other assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the provision of healthcare, MediShield Life addresses most of the general concerns of our seniors.

sections.label: Housing and reverse mortgage
sections.summary: Besides building more HDB studio units for the elderly, the speaker says reverse mortgage should be relooked for all housing types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Besides ramping up the building of HDB studio units for the elderly to facilitate downgrading, we should also relook how we can help the elderly in all housing types, HDB and private residences, to do reverse mortgage.

sections.label: Research funding for elderly technology
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to give more incentives to local researchers to develop technological solutions for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Research funding and grants for this area will yield innovations better suited to our local conditions and elderly residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider providing more incentives to our local researchers to develop technological solutions to better serve and reach out to our seniors.

sections.label: Retaining older workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges retaining public sector older workers until 65, retirement options at 62 or 65, re-employment to 70, and requiring private firms to retain workers until 65.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similarly, I would urge the Government to look at how older workers in the public and Civil Service sectors can be retained in their jobs until 65 and offered re-employment contracts only thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In other words, allow for retirement with two options, that is, one, retire at 62 years old, or, two, retire at 65 years old, and allow for re-employment up to 70 years old.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our seniors should be given more options in deciding their employment in their golden years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also implore the Government to make it a requirement for private companies to retain older workers until the age of 65, and these should be older workers across all ranks and not just those in senior management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Companies that demonstrate strong support in retaining their older workers should be commended and given due recognition.

sections.label: Maintenance of Parents Act declined
sections.summary: The speaker says a woman declined to file a Maintenance Order at the Tribunal under the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When I explained to her that there is a Maintenance of Parents Act, and whether she wishes to file a Maintenance Order at the Tribunal so that her children will give her a higher amount for her maintenance, she swiftly declined.

sections.label: Protecting elderly parents from eviction
sections.summary: The speaker proposes tightening housing policies and possible legislation, similar to the Maintenance of Parents Act, to protect elderly parents who sell their homes to help children and are later neglected or evicted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As I said earlier, with our families getting smaller and with fewer children, the dependence on one or two children will be the norm for each elderly person, and the heartbreak they may face when their only child refuses to take care of them in future or when they get evicted from their shared home, will be very real.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would propose for the Government to look at how our housing policies can be tightened to protect elderly parents who (a) decide to sell their flat or apartment or house; or (b) those who are compelled or maybe even tricked into selling their flat, apartment or house, in order to help their child or children to purchase their own flat, apartment or house.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we respect the decisions of senior or elderly Singaporeans to help their children with their own abode, I would propose that we consider having a policy, or even legislation, that can be invoked to take to task adult children who have benefited from the sale of the abode of their elderly parents and who later on neglect or drive out their parents from the abode they have bought as a result of that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This can be something similar to the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, the adult children can be made to pay back the full amount received from their parents in the purchase of their own abode when their familial relationships fail and eviction of the parents occur, or they can be made to pay for the monthly rental of the elderly parents should the elderly parents take up a rental flat or apartment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, while we have the Maintenance of Parents Act or a new policy or even legislation to protect elderly parents who are made homeless by their own children, surely, we should not need to depend on a piece of legislation that has to be invoked for us to show love, care or responsibility towards our parents.

sections.label: Seniors not on PG package
sections.summary: The speaker hoped PG Ambassadors would also visit seniors not on the PG package, and welcomed the Community Network for Seniors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: During the debate on Budget 2016, I expressed my hope to see seniors who are not on the PG package to be visited by the PG Ambassadors, too, so that they are more aware of the programmes and help available to them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I was, therefore, heartened when Minister Heng announced the Community Network for Seniors.

sections.label: RCs weekly wellness programmes
sections.summary: Over 26 RCs run weekly wellness programmes, with an average of 650 elderly attending.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Today, we have over 26 RCs with weekly wellness programmes, from healthy cooking to exercise classes and health talks, with an average of 650 elderly attending the sessions.

sections.label: PG Ambassadors fall follow-up
sections.summary: PG Ambassadors found a senior with frequent falls and arranged a home fall risk assessment, a ramp and the Disability Assistance Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: But what the PG Ambassadors realised during their visit is that she suffers from frequent falls.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, they followed up with a home fall risk assessment, got a ramp fixed under the HDB's Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme and got her on board the Disability Assistance Scheme.

sections.label: Nursing home without fencing
sections.summary: MOH told the speaker there will be no fencing around the nursing home, with daycare and homecare services available.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Recently, I was delighted to hear from MOH that there will be no fencing around the nursing home and residents can look forward to both daycare and homecare services, such as home nursing and home personal care.

sections.label: New coordinating Ministry proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a new Ministry should be set up to coordinate developments, drive policy and innovation, and implement programmes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Is it time to consider setting up a new Ministry that will be able to coordinate all the developments, drive policy and innovation, and implement the programmes smoothly and efficiently?

sections.label: Active ageing progress in Singapore
sections.summary: The Government with community and public institutions has made steps towards active ageing, which has not yet reached maturity.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, the Government, in partnership with the community and public institutions, have made important steps towards making active ageing a very attractive reality in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: While the issue of active ageing is a never-ending one, it has not yet quite reached maturity.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Like a freshly retired person, there is still some way to go.

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee on Ageing launched a $3 billion Action Plan for Successful Ageing in 2015 with over 70 initiatives across 12 areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Committee on Ageing launched a $3 billion Action Plan for Successful Ageing in 2015 with more than 70 initiatives across 12 areas to achieve this vision.

sections.label: National Silver Academy learning
sections.summary: The National Silver Academy has engaged over 13,000 seniors in more than 900 courses, from IT and media to art and wellness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To support seniors’ interest in learning, we launched the National Silver Academy, which has engaged over 13,000 seniors in learning across more than 900 courses, ranging from information technology (IT) and media courses to art and wellness.

sections.label: CBP volunteers befriending seniors
sections.summary: More than 850 volunteers befriend 2,500 seniors in 47 constituencies under CBP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 850 volunteers befriending 2,500 seniors in 47 constituencies under CBP.

sections.label: Screen for Life subsidies
sections.summary: Eligible Singaporeans now pay no more than $5 for screening and first post-screening consultation at CHAS GP clinics under enhanced Screen for Life subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have also enhanced subsidies under Screen for Life (SFL) to encourage more Singaporeans to go for health screening and follow-up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Now, eligible Singaporeans will only need to pay no more than $5 for screening and the first post-screening consultation at Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) general practitioner (GP) clinics.

sections.label: Home and centre care capacity
sections.summary: Between 2011 and 2017, home and centre care capacity increased by 120% to 13,000 places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Between 2011 and 2017, we have increased the number of home and centre care capacity by 120% to 13,000 places.

sections.label: Respite care and caregiver reliefs
sections.summary: At least 40 nursing homes provide respite care since May 2013, over 1,600 people have used it, and caregivers get tax reliefs up to $14,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: At least 40 nursing homes are providing this service since it was introduced in May 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To date, over 1,600 people have tapped on these respite care services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In the past five years, over 1,200 seniors have been supported through this arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Today, caregivers also benefit from tax reliefs of up to $14,000 for taking care of an elderly parent with a disability.

sections.label: ElderShield Committee interim recommendations
sections.summary: The ElderShield Committee's interim update recommended universal coverage, lower inclusion age of 30, government administration and improved claims assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The ElderShield Committee had provided an interim update last week, with recommendations to make the ElderShield scheme universal for all future cohorts, to lower the inclusion age to 30, for the Government to administer the enhanced ElderShield scheme, and for the claims assessment process to be improved.

sections.label: ElderShield scheme name review
sections.summary: The scheme's name reflects its aim of protecting Singaporeans from long-term care costs, and the Committee will review the name.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The current name of the scheme reflects its objective, which is to protect Singaporeans from the costs of long-term care, in particular, during their older years where the risks of severe disabilities are higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We acknowledge the feedback, however, and the ElderShield Committee will be reviewing the name of the scheme.

sections.label: CNS senior activities and engagement
sections.summary: CNS activated over 70 RCs, engaged over 70,000 seniors, matched 600 befrienders and assisted about 800 seniors with complex needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To date, CNS has activated more than 70 RCs to hold regular preventive health and active ageing activities and engaged more than 70,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: There are now more than 1,500 senior attendances for these programmes on a weekly basis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: CNS has also matched more than 600 seniors to befrienders and assisted about 800 seniors who have complex social and health needs.

sections.label: End-of-life awareness and ageing exhibition
sections.summary: Efforts with community organisations promoted end-of-life and palliative care awareness, and the Dialogue with Time exhibition drew over 10,000 visitors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Together with community-based organisations, we have made efforts to promote awareness of end-of-life issues and palliative care, and we have also launched an exhibition on ageing called Dialogue with Time, at Science Centre, which has attracted over 10,000 visitors since its opening last November.

sections.label: Older residents in labour force
sections.summary: The proportion of residents aged 60 and over in the labour force rose from 6.1% in 2007 to 13.8% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Let us show our love and create a warm society for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the proportion of residents aged 60 and over in our labour force has increased from 6.1% in 2007, to 13.8% in 2017.

sections.label: Re-employment age and RRA support
sections.summary: RRA supports older workers; the re-employment age rose from 65 to 67, and over 98% of eligible private-sector employees were offered re-employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: RRA is to support older workers who want to work longer beyond their retirement age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We took another step forward in 2016 to raise re-employment age from 65 to 67, which has been effective since 1 July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Since it was introduced in 2012, over 98% of private-sector local employees who wished to continue working at age 62 were offered re-employment.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit wage offset
sections.summary: The SEC scheme gives employers a wage offset of up to 8% of monthly wages for employing workers aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme provides a wage offset of up to 8% of monthly wages to employers when they employ older workers aged 55 and above.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant funding
sections.summary: The Work-Life Grant funds each company up to $160,000 over four years to implement FWAs for work and family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Work-Life Grant funds each company up to $160,000 over four years to implement FWAs to help employees better manage work and family responsibilities.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant enhancement
sections.summary: WorkPro was enhanced in July 2016 so companies can receive up to $300,000 under the Job Redesign Grant for older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Second, we should ensure that our jobs are suitably designed and redesigned for our older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: This was why we enhanced the WorkPro in July 2016 to create easier, safer and smarter jobs for older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: A company can now receive up to $300,000, up from $150,000, under the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Since the enhancement, more than 600 companies have applied for the Job Redesign Grant, benefiting more than 9,500 older workers.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Initiative support
sections.summary: Under Adapt and Grow, older PMETs get transition support through PCP and CSP, and Work Trial lets older rank-and-file workers try jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: For instance, under the Adapt and Grow Initiative, older professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) are provided with more support for career or job transition under programmes, such as the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) and Career Support Programme (CSP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Work Trial programme also allows older rank-and-file workers to undergo short-term work trial with companies and acquire new skills to potentially take on new jobs.

sections.label: Digital Readiness Workgroup
sections.summary: MCI supports the Motion and last year convened the Digital Readiness Workgroup to examine status, engage stakeholders and develop strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MCI supports the Motion and last year convened the Digital Readiness Workgroup to examine the current status, engage stakeholders and partners, and to develop strategies relevant to future opportunities and challenges.

sections.label: Silver Infocomm Initiative
sections.summary: MCI, with IMDA and predecessors, has worked over 10 years on user-centric inclusion and skills through the Silver Infocomm Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: First, our programmes, initiatives and products must be user-centric and designed for inclusion of everyone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Second, we must go beyond the provision of access, to equipping people with skills that enable them to participate actively and meaningfully.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MCI, together with the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and its predecessors, has been working on these issues for more than 10 years, through a national programme called the Silver Infocomm Initiative.

sections.label: senior technology familiarity programmes
sections.summary: Programmes in English and vernacular languages have helped 150,000 seniors over 10 years become familiar with technology and connect online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: All of these programmes, and many others, help seniors to become familiar with technology, to develop confidence to conduct transactions and interact online, to connect with one another and their families using digital tools, and to ultimately enjoy the benefits of technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: These programmes are available in English and vernacular languages and, over the last 10 years, have helped 150,000 seniors.

sections.label: Lift upgrading and senior retrofitting
sections.summary: The Lift Upgrading Programme since 2001 gave direct lift access to about 5,200 HDB blocks, and EASE retrofitting has benefited over 130,000 families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP), implemented since 2001, has also provided direct lift access to residents in about 5,200 HDB blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through the City for All Ages and Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programmes, HDB is also retrofitting existing HDB estates and flats with more features, such as grab bars and non-slip toilet flooring, to enhance mobility and comfort for our seniors, benefiting more than 130,000 families thus far.

sections.label: Lease Buyback Scheme for seniors
sections.summary: The Lease Buyback Scheme, introduced in 2009 for lower-income seniors in 3-room or smaller flats, was expanded in 2015 to cover 4-room flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) was introduced in 2009, giving lower-income seniors living in 3-room or smaller flats the option to sell back and monetise the tail-end of their leases to HDB, while continuing to live in their flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The scheme was expanded in 2015 to cover 4-room flats.

sections.label: Banks stopped reverse mortgages
sections.summary: NTUC Income and OCBC bank stopped offering reverse mortgages in 2009 due to a lack of demand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In fact, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Income and Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) bank stopped offering reverse mortgages in 2009, precisely due to a lack of demand.

sections.label: Senior Care leave study
sections.summary: The government is prepared to study Senior Care leave with tripartite partners but should allow businesses time to adjust to recent enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: While we are prepared to study the idea of Senior Care leave in consultation with the tripartite partners, we should allow some time for businesses to adjust and adapt to the recent enhancements.

sections.label: Active Ageing Hubs and services
sections.summary: Services can support evolving needs and put off premature institutionalisation, with plans to build 10 more Active Ageing Hubs by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These services can support them as their needs evolve and put off the need for premature institutionalisation in nursing homes or other facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: There are plans to build another 10 more Active Ageing Hubs by 2020.

sections.label: Senior Cluster Networks and Activity Centres
sections.summary: MSF has set up 19 Senior Cluster Networks and 69 Senior Activity Centres reaching about 30,000 seniors in public rental flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Since 2014, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) has set up 19 Senior Cluster Networks (SCNs), operated by VWOs, to coordinate support for these seniors within each HDB town, with other social and healthcare agencies, including SSOs, Family Service Centres (FSCs) and AIC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The 69 Senior Activity Centres (SACs) reach out to around 30,000 seniors in public rental flats to engage them in recreation and to mitigate social isolation.

sections.label: SSO network for vulnerable seniors
sections.summary: A network of 24 SSOs brings help closer to low-income and vulnerable seniors in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Our network of 24 SSOs has also brought help closer to low-income and vulnerable seniors in the community.

sections.label: Accredited LPA certificate issuers
sections.summary: There are currently 496 medical professionals accredited to be LPA certificate issuers, besides lawyers and psychiatrists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Apart from lawyers and psychiatrists, there are currently 496 medical professionals who are accredited to be LPA certificate issuers.

sections.label: Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme
sections.summary: MSF will launch the Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme this year, letting professionals be remunerated to serve as professional donees and deputies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But we are aware that there are some individuals who may not have next-of-kin who can be appointed as a deputy, or, for that matter, even as a donee, when they make LPAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, MSF will be launching the Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme this year, where professionals can be remunerated for a fee to be appointed as professional donees and deputies.

sections.label: Professional deputies and Comm Kin pilot
sections.summary: Professional deputies can make major decisions such as property liquidation when seniors need institutional care; the Comm Kin pilot begins early this year with two VWOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Professional deputies can step in when the senior requires institutional care, to make more major decisions for the senior, such as liquidation of property, as their expertise would be better suited for such matters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This Comm Kin pilot is expected to begin early this year with two VWOs – TOUCH Community Services and Ang Mo Kio (AMK) FSC Community Services.

sections.label: Vulnerable Adults Bill protection
sections.summary: The Vulnerable Adults Bill will protect individuals 18 and above unable to protect themselves from abuse, neglect or self-neglect, with MSF enhancing partner capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To that end, the Vulnerable Adults Bill, which will be introduced this year, will protect individuals 18 years old and above and, because of mental or physical infirmity, disability or incapacity, are unable to protect themselves from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To complement such legislation, MSF is also working with community partners and stakeholders to enhance the capacity and capabilities of critical players to respond to reports of abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: While this does pose significant challenges, we should plan ahead, prepare well and implement effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Only then can we tap the opportunity that our silver generation brings and turn a perceived challenge into a strength.

sections.label: Whole-of-Government coordination on seniors
